capex.item: Board approved a Preform manufacturing (backward integration) facility with ~INR580 crore capex, initial capacity 300 tons/year (scalable to 500 tons in stage 2), expected to take at least 2 years to come online, targeting 15-20% cost reduction versus buying preform.
capex.quote: The project involves an estimated capital outlay of around ₹580 crore...it will take at least 2 years...it reduces the cost roughly between 15% to 20% of preform.

capex.item: Optical fiber capacity already reached 28 million fkm/year; total cable capacity (including IBR expansion) expected to reach ~45 million fkm-equivalent per year 'very soon'.
capex.quote: our strategy of increasing our capacity for fiber, which we have already taken to 28 million fiber kilometres per year, and cable, which will very soon become 45 million fiber kilometre equivalent cable per year.

capex.item: Board approved (July 11, 2025) IBR cable capacity expansion from ~1.73 million fkm/annum to ~19.01 million fkm/annum at Hyderabad and Goa, taking total OFC capacity from ~25.08 to ~42.36 million fkm/annum, to be fully completed by end of June 2026.
capex.quote: our total optical fibre cable manufacturing capacity will increase from ~25.08 million fibre kilometers to ~42.36 million fibre kilometres per annum...it will be completed before the end of June 26.

capex.item: Poland OFC plant (~3.5 million fkm capacity, ~INR145 crore capex) expected to be commercialized within calendar year 2025, roughly nine months out from the call.
capex.quote: Project, we would expect this to be commercialized in within the calendar year '25... a little more than that, nine months, something like that.

capex.item: Tactical cable manufacturing capacity being increased from 3 to 5 machines, with backward integration into steel-tube manufacturing planned.
capex.quote: We have three machines at the point for tactical cable, which we are increasing to five.

capex.item: IBR (intermittently bonded ribbon) cable manufacturing capacity being more than doubled to serve rising data-center cable demand.
capex.quote: we are increasing our capacity to manufacture IBR cables. We are almost more than doubling that capacity.

capex.item: Poland optical fiber cable plant (3.25 million fkm initial capacity, expandable to 7 million fkm) targeted to start manufacturing from April of next financial year (FY25).
capex.quote: 3.25 million capacity, we are targeting to start manufacturing from April of next financial year.

capex.item: Final decision on setting up an in-house preform plant (backward integration) expected in the next one to two months.
capex.quote: maybe in next one or two months' time we will take a final decision.

capex.item: Fiber capacity expansion (Hyderabad) expected to be completed by 31st March 2025.
capex.quote: That capacity expansion of fiber would be completed by more or less by 31st March 2025.

capex.item: OFC cable capacity to rise from 30.5 to 42.36 million fkm by June 2026; optical fiber capacity (already doubled from 14 to 28 million fkm) to add balance ~6 million fkm progressively by December 2026.
capex.quote: Optical Fibre Cable capacity will rise from 30.5 mn fkm to 42.36 mn fkm by June 2026...with the balance 6 mn fkm to be added progressively by December 2026.

capex.item: Foundation stone for the Andhra Pradesh ammunition factory (first product: Multi-Mode Hand Grenade) to be laid on 15th May 2026 by the Defense Minister and Andhra CM; budgeted capex ~INR125 crores this year (land+building) plus ~INR250 crores over next 2 years.
capex.quote: 15th of May, foundation stone will be laid down for these two factories...budgeted about INR125 crores for this facility...next 2 years would be another INR250 crores.

capex.item: Optical fiber capacity to increase from 28 to 33.9 million fkm by December 2026; optical fiber cable capacity to increase from 34 to 39 million fkm by July 2026 and to 42.36 million fkm by December 2026.
capex.quote: Our current Optical Fibre capacity of 28 mn fkm is expected to increase to 33.9 mn fkm by December 2026...to reach 39 fkm by July 2026 and to reach 42.36 mn fkm by December 2026.

deepdive.thesis: HFCL delivered record Q4/FY26 performance driven by explosive export growth (41% of revenue), hyperscale data center demand, and defense aerospace acquisition, with structural margin expansion expected from preform backward integration and high-value product mix shift — this transforms HFCL from a cyclical EPC player into a globally competitive, high-margin technology manufacturer with multi-year visibility.

open.item: UP Jal Nigam project execution slowed due to non-payment by state government (which itself was awaiting central government funds); UP CM has now promised state funding to unblock this.
Of the INR10,480 crore order book, approximately INR3,000 crores expected to be executed/converted to revenue within FY26.
OFC business revenue expected to more than double in FY26 versus FY25 (specifically ~INR2,400 crores vs INR1,200 crores last year), with more than 50% of that from exports.

Management explicitly admitted the PLI amount previously expected (~INR40-50 crores in FY26, guided in Q3FY25) will NOT be received, because indigenous telecom-product revenue commitment level was not reached; also no PLI expected in FY26.
Total capex for FY26 estimated at roughly INR250 crores, of which ~INR130 crores towards IBR cable expansion.
BharatNet Phase III revenue for FY26 expected at roughly INR800-1,000 crores (about 20% of the ~INR5,000 crore total order).
Total capex of about INR900 crores planned over the next 2 years (FY25-FY26), funded via internal accruals, prior equity raise and part debt.
HFCL received notice to submit its upgraded BMP-2 armament sample for Army evaluation by 26th June 2026 (sample already sent to Babina firing range).
The landmark ~USD1.1 billion (~INR10,159 crore) long-term global OFC hyperscaler supply contract execution expected to begin around end of Q1FY27.
Electronic fuzes require further upgrade following the Balasore trial; retesting expected in 'a couple of months' — a further slip from the April 2026 date given in Q3FY26.

HFCL qualified (DRDO tech transfer complete, aging certificate done) to participate in a large multi-mode hand grenade Army tender expected to open in about 1-1.5 months; only 3 licensees exist and 2 of 3 will win orders.
EPC/turnkey business (loss-making due to the NFS Army network warranty period) expected to turn profitable once the NFS AMC contract is signed, expected around Q2FY27.
NFS project receivables (~INR400 crores outstanding) expected to be fully collected/mitigated by mid of FY27, reducing working capital and interest cost.

Board approved (March 25, 2026) acquisition of an aerospace defense business under subsidiary HFCL Advance Systems, with an export-oriented order book of ~INR1,930 crores; definitive agreements to be executed on/before May 31, 2026, closing expected within calendar year 2026.

Optical fiber capacity to increase from 28 to 33.9 million fkm by December 2026; optical fiber cable capacity to increase from 34 to 39 million fkm by July 2026 and to 42.36 million fkm by December 2026.
Defense (largely aerospace plus land systems) expected to contribute roughly 10-12% of total FY27 revenue.
FY27 revenue growth expected (management stresses 'expectation not guidance') at around 20-25% over FY26's ~INR4,949-5,000 crores base, i.e. roughly INR6,000-6,250 crores.

Blended EBITDA margin expected to expand by 3-4 percentage points in FY27 versus FY26 (~18.5%), driven by product mix, defense/data-center high-margin revenue, and EPC turnkey losses (NFS warranty drag) reversing.
EPC/turnkey revenue guided down to roughly INR1,000 crores next year (FY27) versus ~INR1,500 crores this year, as management intentionally deprioritizes EPC in favor of defense/OFC/telecom equipment.
Telecom products (routers, UBR, FWA CPE etc.) revenue expected at roughly INR500 crores next year (FY27).

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
